newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai MPs propose rate cuts to spur economy.
newsitem.headline: Thai MPs propose rate cuts to spur economy.

text.p: Two leading Thai opposition MPs called on the government to help weak exports by inducing lower interest rates and spur housing demand by raising tax relief.

Former finance minister Tarrin Nimmanahaeminda said late on Saturday that the Bank of Thailand's current policy of keeping Thai interest rates high to attract foreign capital inflow has been pursued at the expense of private business.

"It is ironic that the government tries to stabilise the economy by keeping interest rates high but leaves the private sector to suffer," he told a function organised by the opposition Democrat Party.

Tarrin said the government, whose sovereign credit ratings are stronger than the Thai private sector, should tab foreign loans and use them to indirectly inject funds into the economy to ease burdens faced by the private sector.
Prime lending rates quoted by Thai banks are among the highest in the region, averaging 13.25-13.75 percent, while those offered by finance companies are several percentage points higher.
Former deputy prime minister Supachai Panichpakdi, also a Democrat, said the government lacked focus in tackling export and property sector problems.

He told businessmen and diplomats at the function that the government should extend 30-year concessional housing loans to the public instead of keeping its 50-billion-baht ($1.9 billion) property reviving fund for the benefit of civil servants.
The property sector is reeling under a four-year slump with no quick recovery in sight. Property gluts have shaken financial institutions exposed to the sector.

Supachai said the government economic team led by current Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan has not done enough to boost exports, which contracted 0.2 percent in 1996 after expanding more than 20 percent a year for most of this decade.

"It should set up a war room to look at export problems on a daily basis. It should target specific export products to promote instead of sending general trade missions abroad. Trade talks should be conducted bilaterally to get real results instead of going through the World Trade Organisation," he said.
